AMC also argued that the vehicles which it produces, fourwheel drive, general utility jeep-type vehicles should be placed in a separate class because these vehicles were inherently less fuel economical than nonpassenger automobiles in general.
After considering these comments, as well as comments from International Harvester and Ford relating to separate classification, the agency has decided to establish a separate class for four-wheel drive, jeep-type vehicles. Because the agency intends that only four-wheel drive jeep-type vehicles, and not other four-wheel drive vehicles, such as some pickup trucks, be eligible for the separate class, the agency will allow only vehicles with wheelbases less than 110 inches to be eligible for the separate class. Each manufacturer of jeep-type vehicles will have the option of including those vehicles in the separate class, or including those vehicles in the general class of nonpassenger automobiles. In this way, the problems of both the manufacturer with a broad product line and the manufacturer with a narrow product line can be accommodated consistent with the purposes of Title V.
